_comment: EN translation of tracks/image/products/playground.md body; keys aligned with zh structure. Facts unchanged; verification dates as in zh.

axes.model_access: Third-party model aggregation is the current state: the homepage names GPT Image 2, Nano Banana Pro, Nano Banana and Seedream (direct-fetched today); the in-house model line (Playground v2/v2.5/v3) has been discontinued — the official 2025-01 cut of the legacy product line (third-party review account); what is sold now is mainly access to other companies' models (credits consumed per model).
axes.runtime: Web (playground.com → playgroundai.com) + iOS app (App Store link on record, 4.9/5 across 5,400+ ratings); generation and design editing run on the vendor's cloud; no local runtime surface.
axes.local_files: Designs and assets live on the account side in the cloud; print merch (T-shirts/stickers etc.) goes through the platform's ordering surface; no official statement found for a local data surface or an export-then-edit-locally line (details not verified line by line).
axes.background: Instant generation + editor (Smart Layers non-destructive editing, Extract Text into editable layers, homepage on record); no persistent-task / resume-when-off surface (no statement verified); templates across 24 categories (homepage on record).
axes.tools: The design workbench is the core: template customization, Smart Layers, swap-style/remove-object/add-mockup tools (homepage on record), a print-merch store; not a pure image generator — the official positioning is "The AI design studio for everyone" (homepage on record), competing with Canva-style design tools.
axes.context: Organized around projects/design files; cross-session memory not verified in any official statement. The template + layer system is its consistency mechanism, not memory.
axes.permissions: Free + subscription (D9: prices not collected); the terms expressly disclaim copyrightability and uniqueness of outputs and put rights-clearing for commercial use on the user; public assets are viewable and remixable by others by default, and granted licenses survive termination (per terms); the DMCA agent is a third party, JACO Product Development, LLC (per terms).
axes.fit: Fits: finished-design flows (stickers/T-shirts/posters/logos), template + layer editing workflows, several generation models behind one interface. Not a fit: wanting an in-house model line (it pivoted to third-party aggregation), wanting output-copyright certainty (the terms expressly disclaim it), enterprise compliance narratives.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the post-pivot official pages do not give):

- **Actual credit burn across models (GPT Image 2 vs Nano Banana vs Seedream)**
- **Editability of Smart Layers exports** (PSD/SVG or bitmap only)
- **The actual default state of public-asset visibility** (the terms say public and remixable by default)
unknowns:
- The acquirer's identity (the founder confirmed the sale in 2026-06 without naming the buyer; third-party account)
- Where the in-house model weights went (v2/v2.5 were once open under community licenses; current status unverified)
- The publication date of the official blog post "Next Chapter" (specific date not verified today)
- The cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
- The quota gap between the old and new free tiers (third-party reviews say old paid plans were auto-refunded in 2025-01; official wording unverified)
related: Both are aggregator-style "templates + generation" design benches: Designer is tied to the Microsoft ecosystem, Playground to third-party models + print merch.
Cross-category contrast: the flagship model on Playground's homepage, GPT Image 2, sits in ChatGPT's parent product line.
